data.title: Slider
data.tagline: Drag to adjust a value within a range
data.description: A slider is useful for quickly changing volume, brightness, or a price range. Show the limits and current value, and make the control work from the keyboard. If an exact number matters, pair it with an Number Input.

use: A value where relative position is useful
avoid: Ask for an exact value without displaying it
Use a narrow track for a very large range
Hide the minimum and maximum when they matter
Require dragging as the only accessible input method

lessonPractice.title: Player volume runs continuously from 0 to 100, must update while dragging, and must work from a keyboard. How should it be designed?

options.label: Use a slider that shows its value, previews changes live, and responds to arrow keys
options.feedback: Volume is a continuous range. A visible value, live feedback, and keyboard controls cover both understanding and operation.

options.label: Provide only a number field and update volume after entry loses focus
options.feedback: A number field supports precision but removes the continuous adjustment and immediate listening required here.

options.label: Put every integer from 0 to 100 in a dropdown and update after selection
options.feedback: A long fixed list increases search effort and cannot provide feedback throughout a continuous drag.

data.agentPrompt: Build volume as a 0–100 slider with a continuously visible value, live audio updates while dragging, and arrow-key support. Test mouse, touch, and keyboard input, and do not wait until drag end to apply the value.
